H1.text: Jump off a boat, and the boat slides back. Push off a friend on skates, and you both roll away.

H2.text: Nobody pushed from outside, yet everything moves.

H3.text: At the ice rink, Diya sees two skaters at rest, face to face. They push off each other.

H4.text: One glides left, one glides right. Where did all this momentum come from?

H5.text: The answer is: from nowhere. Let's see why.

P1.text: First, a system of particles is a group of bodies we look at together.

P2.text: Here, the system is the two skaters. Each has a momentum: mass times velocity.

P3.text: Add them as vectors, and you get the total momentum, capital P.

P4.text: Forces between the skaters are inside forces. A push from anything else, like a coach, is outside.

S1.text: To the motion notebook. Skater A is forty kilograms, skater B is sixty. Both at rest.

S2.text: So the total momentum is zero. The gold cross marks the centre of mass.

S3.text: They push. A glides left at three metres per second. B glides right at two.

S4.text: A carries minus one hundred and twenty. B carries plus one hundred and twenty. The total is still zero.

S5.text: On the graph, A falls, B rises, and the total stays flat on zero. The gold cross does not move.

S6.text: Slow-mo replay. Freeze in the middle of the push.

S7.text: A pushes B. B pushes A back. Equal forces, opposite ways, for the same time.

S8.text: So whatever momentum B gets, A gets the same, the other way. Inside forces cancel in pairs.

S9.text: Now they pull each other in on a rope. Will the total momentum change? Pause and decide.

S10.text: No! The pull is an inside force too. The total stays zero, and they meet at the centre of mass.

D1.text: Now let's write the law, one step at a time.

D2.text: Step one. Add every momentum as vectors. P equals p one, plus p two, and so on, up to p n.

D3.text: Step two. Each p is m times v. The sum of all the m v is M V: total mass times the velocity of the centre of mass.

D4.text: Step three. How fast P changes each second, d P by d t, equals the sum of all the forces.

D5.text: Inside forces come in equal, opposite pairs, so they add to zero. Only the outside force is left.

D6.text: So d P by d t equals F external. With no outside force, P stays constant, and the centre of mass keeps a steady velocity.

T1.text: Remember this. Only an outside force can change the total momentum of a system.

R1.text: Now, why does the lighter skater glide faster? Link by link.

R2.text: P starts at zero, and no outside force acts. So it stays zero.

R3.text: So A's momentum and B's momentum must be equal in size, and opposite in direction.

R4.text: Forty times three equals sixty times two. Less mass, more speed. That is why a light boat shoots back fast.

K1.text: Side by side. Inside forces: the skaters push each other, and the total stays zero.

K2.text: Outside force: a coach pushes the pair with fifty newtons for two seconds. The total grows to one hundred.

K3.text: Now you try. You sit in a cart and push hard on its front wall. Will the cart roll forward? Pause and decide.

K4.text: No! You and the cart are one system. Your push is an inside force, so the total stays zero.

W2.text: Three balls on a smooth floor: one kilogram at six metres per second east, two kilograms at three west, three kilograms at two north. Find P, and the centre of mass velocity.

W3.text: Along x: one times six is plus six. Two times three, west, is minus six. Zero.

W4.text: Along y: three times two. Six kilogram metres per second, north.

W5.text: So P is six, north. The total mass is six kilograms.

W6.text: V equals P over M. Six over six. One metre per second, north.

X2.text: Many students think: zero total momentum means nothing is moving.

X3.text: Not true. Both skaters move, but their momenta cancel. Zero total means only that the centre of mass is at rest.

E1.text: Where is this asked? Centre of mass velocity, explosions, and inside versus outside forces.

Q1.text: Exam level now. Two kilograms at three i plus two j metres per second. Three kilograms at minus two j. A spring joins them. An outside force of five j newtons acts for two seconds. Speed of the centre of mass? Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is B. Two metres per second.

A2.text: At the start, P is six i plus four j, minus six j. That is six i minus two j.

A3.text: The spring is inside, so ignore it. The outside force adds ten j. P becomes six i plus eight j.

A4.text: Its size is ten. Divide by the total mass, five kilograms. Two metres per second.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these without help?

Y2.text: One. Two skaters at rest push apart. Why does the total momentum stay zero?

Y3.text: Two. How is the total momentum linked to the centre of mass?

Y4.text: Three. Which forces can change the total momentum of a system?

N1.text: Next time: turn a screw with a spanner. You push sideways, yet the screw goes straight in. We meet the vector cross product.
